title: Qt: Add automatic profile switching
description:
Add the ability to automatically switch profiles based on display
filters. Add an "Auto Switch Filter" column to the Configuration
Profiles dialog which lets the user associate a display filter with a
profile. When loading a capture file, switch to the first profile with a
matching filter.

Example of the Configuration Profiles dialog with this change:

![profile-filters](/uploads/46f46bb3d5b8376cf93a91218687a8b1/profile-filters.png)

Can the "Auto Switch Filter" preference be moved to a new profile related preferences page instead of added to this dialog? I'm worried that this dialog will be cluttered with all kind of values ("author", description, repo, URL, etc.).

Even though the new profile settings allows for extra fields, I don't plan on adding any more any time soon.

I agree with you concerns about clutter.
If someone does want to add extra fields, it might make sense to switch to a layout similar to the main preferences window, where you have a list of profiles on the left and various settings on the right.

The implementation has some issues.

1. It's not possible to create a new profile with a filter, the filter must be added later
2. Duplicate/Copy a profile does not copy the filter
3. After renaming a profile the filter is removed from the table
4. After renaming a profile it's not possible to set/change the filter
5. It's not possible to delete the filter
6. It's possible to set the filter to one space, but this will crash when opening a capture file (in `dfilter_prime_proto_tree()`).

I think all of this will be avoided if having the configuration in a separate preferences page.

> 1. It's not possible to create a new profile with a filter, the filter must be added later

How do you envision this working?
If I create or copy a filter a new item is created with an active QLineEdit for the profile name.
We can't have two active QLineEdits at this point.
When I'm done changing the name I can double-click the filter column, which doesn't seem to be too onerous.

> 2. Duplicate/Copy a profile does not copy the filter

This is the preferred behavior, to me at least.
If we copy the filter, the user will end up with two profiles with the same filter.
That doesn't seem to be very useful.

> 3. After renaming a profile the filter is removed from the table
> 4. After renaming a profile it's not possible to set/change the filter
> 5. It's not possible to delete the filter
> 6. It's possible to set the filter to one space, but this will crash when opening a capture file (in dfilter_prime_proto_tree()).

Fixed.

1. When I create a new profile, or copy an existing profile, I can change the profile name but I cannot set a filter. I need to close the Profiles dialog (`Ok` to create the new profile) and then open the Profiles dialog again to be able to set a filter.
2. Ok, this makes sense.

Should we have a preference to "Use auto switch filters" to be able to disable this feature without having to remove all configured filters? I can envision this as a use case.
7. `Cancel` does not revert the changes done to filters.

> 1. When I create a new profile, or copy an existing profile, I can change the profile name but I cannot set a filter. I need to close the Profiles dialog (`Ok` to create the new profile) and then open the Profiles dialog again to be able to set a filter.

This should be fixed.

> Should we have a preference to "Use auto switch filters" to be able to disable this feature without having to remove all configured filters? I can envision this as a use case.

The problem with adding a preference is that you would have to add it to all profile preferences. We might be able to work around that by adding a setting to the default personal profile. I've added a comment to that effect.

> 7. `Cancel` does not revert the changes done to filters.

Fixed.

Thanks for testing and reviewing this!

Something feels wrong with the column resize. If I expand the `Profile` column and select a different profile the column is resized back.

I would like the `Profile` column to use most space if `Auto Switch Filter` is empty or have short filters.

The previous code called `setStretchLastSection(false)` and `setSectionResizeMode(ProfileModel::COL_NAME, QHeaderView::Stretch)`. This ensured a wide name column, but it made the resize behavior really weird IMHO. This disabled resizing the name column, and in order to resize one of the other two columns I had to grab the right sizer handle and move the mouse in the direction opposite of what I was expecting.

I switched to leaving stretchLastSection enabled and calling `resizeColumnToContents` for COL_NAME and COL_TYPE. I also overrode `sizeHintForColumn` so that it returned a wide value for COL_NAME if we don't have a wide filter. I think this gives us a nice compromise between the name column behavior you're looking for and making column resizing behave like the rest our UI.

> If I expand the `Profile` column and select a different profile the column is resized back.

We were calling `resizeColumnToContents(ProfileModel::COL_NAME)` in several places, including `updateWidgets`. The latest MR now only resizes in the constructor.

The updates are better. I would still like the `Auto Switch Filter` to only be as wide as the header when no profile use this feature, but this may be just my personal preference.

![Screenshot_2024-04-02_at_09.53.47](/uploads/a5264513834cb84a58b0f7158e56c846/Screenshot_2024-04-02_at_09.53.47.png)

changed this line in [version 13 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/15015/diffs?diff_id=970665106&start_sha=1af4f9d8e50b459624cd039937900de392f399cf#e3ea05a170386617c0ef52342fbe587f3f8c5b86_463_463)
Fixed.

I still find some issues which I think should be fixed before merge:
* It's not possible to switch to the `Default` profile when having an open capture file and a profile is auto selected. It is possible to switch to a different profile, just not the `Default`.
* I get the `dfilter_prime_proto_tree()` crash again after removing a filter for a profile. The `profile_settings` file contains an empty `auto_switch_filter: ` entry in this case.

When loading a big pcap file a profile is not always auto selected, even if the first packet matches the filter (I use `udp` as filter). I don't know exactly when this happens.

> * It's not possible to switch to the `Default` profile when having an open capture file and a profile is auto selected. It is possible to switch to a different profile, just not the `Default`.

I'm having trouble duplicating this. When you try to switch to the `Default` profile, does it automatically switch back to the same profile? If so, the filename logic at the top of `ProfileSwitcher::checkPacket` might be faulty. Otherwise I'm not sure what's going on.

> * I get the `dfilter_prime_proto_tree()` crash again after removing a filter for a profile. The `profile_settings` file contains an empty `auto_switch_filter:` entry in this case.

I was adding a NULL dfcode to the filter list. This should be fixed now.

> When loading a big pcap file a profile is not always auto selected, even if the first packet matches the filter (I use `udp` as filter). I don't know exactly when this happens.

I was hooking into `PacketList::rowsInserted` before, which isn't necessarily called for the first few packets. I switched to hooking into `PacketListModel::appendPacket` instead.

It turns out that the issue I reported with the `Default` profile is from a Lua plugin I have which does `reload_packets()` if preferences have changed when `proto.prefs_changed()` is called. The Lua plugin is a FileHandler using preferences to control how to read the file, and a reload is required when the preferences change (it doesn't known if this file handler is used).

From this I found that the auto switch also happens when you reload the file. If you manually change from the auto selected profile and reload the file, the auto switch will happen again. I'm not sure if this should be considered as a bug or a feature. Maybe we need a `capture_file.reloading` flag?

The latest change enables automatic switching if the current capture file path is different from the most recent capture file path and if we haven't manually switched our profile. It shouldn't be too difficult to change that logic if needed.

Now the auto switch does not work after the first manual profile switch. It doesn't auto switch if I close and open the same file, and sometimes if I close and open a different file. I haven't found the pattern.

That seems to match the currently documented behavior except for "sometimes if I close and open a different file":

> When you open a capture file, Wireshark will check each filter against the first 1000 packets and will switch to the first profile with a matching filter.
Manually changing your profile will disable this behavior until you open a different capture file.

I made the switching logic depend on two bools (capture_file_changed_ and profile_changed_); hopefully that will make it easier to keep the actual and documented behavior in alignment.

The current behavior assumes that if you're at the welcome screen with no captures open and you switch profiles, that you want your choice to stick, which is why the code currently disables switching in that case.

I'm going to go ahead and merge this so that we can get feedback on the switching behavior and the feature in general from more people. A couple of possible improvements I can think of are:

- Showing an indicator in the status bar when switching is enabled.
- Flashing the status bar when a new profile is applied.
`MAX_SETTINGS_TOKENS` is now unused.

commits_data.title: Qt: Add automatic profile switching
commits_data.message:
Qt: Add automatic profile switching

Add the ability to automatically switch profiles based on display
filters. Add an "Auto Switch Filter" column to the Configuration
Profiles dialog which lets the user associate a display filter with a
profile. Add a "gui.profile_switch_check_count" which determines the
number of packets or events to check.

When loading a capture file, switch to the first profile with a matching
filter.

Add a short description to the User's Guide. Hold off on updating
ws-gui-config-profiles.png until we're sure the UI is stable.

Ping #10352, #14226
